title: Apache-2.0 chosen over MIT or GPL for patent grant
context: OpenKaava is a container that runs third-party tools. The license must protect both the core and the tool ecosystem.
decision: OpenKaava uses Apache-2.0, not MIT or GPL. Apache-2.0 includes an explicit patent grant. MIT says nothing about patents. GPL and AGPL copyleft would give someone a real argument that private tools mounting into OpenKaava are derivative works.
consequences: Apache-2.0 protects patent rights while avoiding copyleft complications. Third-party commercial tools can be mounted without legal ambiguity. The codebase is freely copyable and forkable, but the name is a trademark not covered by the license.
